To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the predictors of employment for recently arrived refugee migrant (RAM) men are: region of birth, length in time in Australia, English language proficiency, recognition of overseas qualifications, seeking employment through formal and informal networks and having access to a vehicle.
the employment rate of refugee men increased from 44% to 56% over the two years of the study.

(a) region of birth, length in Australia, seeking help from job service providers and social networks, and owning cars were significant predictors of the likelihood of finding a job; (b) English language proficiency was a significant predictor of finding a job, but only in the first six months of the study; (c) recognition of overseas qualifications and experience decreased the likelihood of finding employment; and (d) employment increased over time.
